segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, quick forecast check. For Riverbend, I moved the 42-seat add-on to commit at $18,480 annual, start date September 1. Procurement sent back the insurance language but no price issue.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Okay. Did deal desk approve the ramp, or is it still the flat seat count on the pricing sheet?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Approved this morning. First invoice is 14 seats for September, then 28 more on November 1. Billing tool can handle it, I just need the signed order form by Friday.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Good. Can you sanity-check Pine Hill while you're in there? Billing tool shows service through 7/31, and the CRM's last customer touch is the May QBR. I wasn't sure whether to leave their August seats in the run rate.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Uh, yeah, I'll look after this call. I was heads down on the municipal renewal and missed that queue.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: No worries. Municipal is the $32,600 one with the two-year term, right?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep. Starts October 15, 63 users, same support tier. They asked for net 45, finance said okay if they pay the open $4,210 invoice first.

segments.speaker: Colleague
segments.text: Makes sense. Anything else weird in your number?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Not weird. Baxter is sliding from August 20 to September 3 for go-live because their admin is out, but contract is signed and the seats are already provisioned.
